title: Lossy KV cache compression playbook: controlled FP8/INT8/INT4 experiments and rollback policies
creator: Ava Sharma
description: Goal: produce a reproducible playbook and measurement suite for applying lossy compression to the KV cache (FP8/INT8/INT4) that balances GPU memory savings against per-token fidelity for long-context workloads. We want concrete fallback and rollout rules so the runtime can opportunistically compress KV shards while preserving user-visible quality SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end Jupyter + script-driven experiment that runs on both A100-80GB and H100-80GB images
Quantization transforms for per-layer and per-shard modes: symmetric int8, asymmetric int8, shared scale FP8, per-row int4 with zero-point
Automatic generation of token-level fidelity metrics: KL per-token, normalized surprisal delta, and top-1 token disagreement rate
A suggested runtime decision policy (rules + thresholds) and a simple fallback plan that can be implemented in runtime-1.23
Benchmarked memory savings (MB) and throughput impact (tokens/s) for continuous batching windows 50ms/100ms/200ms
experiment_plan: Baseline collection: run representative prompt suites (chat, code, summarization) instrumented for token traces and KV sizes with uncompressed FP16 KV cache

Compression modes to test: per-layer FP8 (shared mantissa), per-shard asymmetric int8, blockwise int4 (4-bit packing with local scale), and hybrid schemes combining FP8 for deep layers and int4 for attention heads 0..N
Calibration: collect per-layer activation statistics from warm runs (1k sequences) to compute scale and bias; store calibration tables in Drive for reproducibility
Workloads: 8K-context long-form dialogue, 32K-window summarization, and 2K code synthesis with frequent resets to exercise caching behavior
Hardware: A100-80GB (baseline) and H100-80GB (target) with CUDA 12.x and cuBLAS/cuDNN tuned; run multiple seeds to capture variance
Measurements: token-level KL vs baseline, cumulative perplexity increase, top-k token disagreement, end-to-end latency P50/P95, throughput tokens/s under continuous batching windows
Stress tests: simulate KV eviction and shard rehydration under memory pressure and measure rollback latency and quality impact
Safety net: instrumentation to automatically revert to FP16 for shards where loss exceeds threshold or if hallucination score crosses warning band
results_summary: Preliminary results (first 48h): per-layer FP8 reduced KV memory by ~2.6x on average with token KL median increase below 0.02 on chat workloads; int4 aggressive packing delivered up to 4.1x memory reduction but exhibited heavy tail degradation on long-context (>12k tokens)

Throughput: hybrid FP8/int4 profiles increased effective tokens/s by ~1.6x under continuous batching 100ms on A100; H100 showed similar trends but with slightly higher variance likely due to kernel selection differences
Failure modes observed: int4 block packing occasionally introduced high local distortion in early tokens after cache rehydration leading to repeated attention drift observed in code generation traces

Rollback times: cold rehydration (fetch full FP16 shard from persistent store) averaged 220-480ms depending on shard size; we prototyped an incremental rehealing path that reduced visible regression by streaming partial FP16 tiles within 90-160ms

Quality trade-offs: for customer-impact-sensitive routes (assistant chat, policy queries) we recommend conservative FP8-only profiles with per-shard monitoring; for background batch embedding or internal reranking, int8/int4 hybrid provides better cost savings
updates: 2026-03-02: Collected baseline traces for chat and code suites. Noted that KV shape distribution is skewed: last 4 layers account for >55% of KV memory.
2026-03-04: Implemented calibration runner in notebook: drive link uploaded. Early FP8 symmetric gave stable SNR across layers but needed per-layer scale refinement.
2026-03-06: First int4 prototype committed (PR #4027). Observed tail degradations during cache roll-ins; added additional checks to guard first N tokens after rehydration.
2026-03-09: Hooked experiment dashboard to runtime QA traces. P95 latency regression acceptable for non-interactive routes; interactive routes require throttling of compression actions.
2026-03-13: Drafted runtime decision policy and rollback playbook; opened RFC for runtime team (RFC-ckv-compression) and created action items for Dedicated autoscaler integration
notes: Next steps: validate hybrid policy on 32K-context experimental cluster, bake per-shard telemetry into Console rollout charts, and add canary flag for per-tenant opt-in.
Open question: whether to prefer asymmetric int8 vs per-row 4-bit packing for attention-heavy heads — needs headwise ablation on code workloads.
Design constraint: any runtime fallback must avoid user-visible token reordering; streaming partial rehydration preferred over immediate full revert when possible.
